title: Partnership Review Mini-Kit & Renewal Tracker
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic QBR deck template aimed at short executive alignment meetings (20-30m) and a lightweight renewal tracker to run alongside. Focus: surfacing the minimal set of signals that drive a renewal decision and defining concrete next-step asks. This is a working draft—meant to be copied and tailored per account.

Audience:
- CSMs preparing executive touchpoints
- AMs and Renewal Managers validating commercial scenarios
- SEs who provide quick technical demos for fixes

High-level approach (design principles):
- One-sentence health + one-number signal (the "Renewal Pulse") up top
- Limit deck to 6 slides for standard accounts, 10+ for enterprise
- Always end with an explicit checkbox-style decision (renew/hold/require action)
- Pair the deck with a single-row tracker card per account for stage and owner clarity

Deck outline (compact 6-slide starter):
1) Cover & Objective (slide 1)
   - Customer, date, objective: "Decision: recommended renewal outcome"
   - Meeting length and expected participants
2) Renewal Pulse (slide 2)
   - 0-10 pulse number (visual bar), one-line rationale (e.g., "7: solid adoption, exec not engaged")
   - Renewal date window and target ask (renew/expand/short-term hold)
3) Top 2 outcome metrics (slide 3)
   - Metric / baseline / current / delta (three bullets)
   - Quick interpretation line on business impact
4) Friction & reliability (slide 4)
   - Top 3 support/incidents in last 90 days and measurable impact (minutes, failed jobs, etc.)
   - Where we are blocking value (one-sentence each)
5) Commercial scenarios (slide 5)
   - Minimal renewal, modest expansion, committed renewal + discount (1-line each)
   - Key commercial ask and decision timeline
6) Clear next steps & owners (slide 6)
   - Action list with owners and due dates; explicit executive decision row

Enterprise expansion (add-on slides):
- ROI snapshot with modeled NPV for proposed expansion (3-year view)
- Compliance/SLA commitments and timelines
- Rollout plan: phases, launch owners, milestone dates
- Legal / procurement checklist if renewal > threshold

Renewal Pulse: a simple ladder (0-10) and how to compute it quickly in the field
- Inputs (fast proxies):
  - Usage ratio (0-4): current active usage / expected usage target
  - Outcome momentum (0-3): whether customer KPIs moved in direction we committed to
  - Engagement quality (0-3): exec touches, roadmap syncs, support backlog clearance
- Manual override allowed with note (e.g., exec champion left -> -2 override)
- Triage: 0-3 = High risk, 4-6 = Watch, 7-10 = Healthy

Renewal triggers matrix (one-page):
- Trigger examples that push an account to "intervene":
  - Any P1 outage that impacted revenue
  - Exec sponsor change AND no replacement within 30 days
  - >25% drop in key request volume vs prior quarter

Lightweight tracker: suggested columns (one-row-per-account card)
- Account | Renewal date | Renewal Pulse | Risk Tier | CSM | AM | Last Exec Meeting | Commercial Ask | Next Milestone | Owner | Status | Short Notes
- Status values: green/monitor/at-risk/escalted

Sample commercial options phrasing (concise lines for slide):
- Baseline renewal: unchanged seats, 12-month term, no discount
- Committed renewal: 12-month + 10% seat increase, 5% commit discount
- Strategic partner package: 24-month term, tiered pricing, dedicated onboarding credits

60/30/14 Rapid Playbook (for Watch/At-risk accounts)
- Day 60: Align on root cause + exec summary
  - Deliverable: 1-page "What failed, why, proposal"
  - Who: CSM + AM + SE + SRE as needed
- Day 30: Demonstrate fixes + monitor metrics
  - Deliverable: Live demo or recorded screen and metric snapshot
  - Who: CSM (exec sponsor), SE (tech fix), SRE (reliability patches)
- Day 14: Final decision prep & executive ask
  - Deliverable: Decision checklist and approval note from customer execs
  - Who: AM (commercial close) + CSM

Templates & canned language (short):
- Exec invite subject: "Partnership flash review & decision  [Customer] — 25 min"
- Exec invite body: "Quick partnership pulse + proposed renewal ask. Goal: confirm path by [date]."
- Post-meeting follow-up subject: "[Customer]  Brief notes + decisions"
- Follow-up bullets: what happened, owner, due date, next sync

Role matrix (one-liner responsibilities):
- CSM: owns the pulse, compiles deck, leads technical/operational remediation
- AM: owns the commercial ask and negotiations
- SE: provides demo/fix and integration plan
- SRE/Product: scope and deliver reliability commitments
- Renewal Manager: final approval for concessions and escalations

Success metrics to measure kit impact (suggested):
- % of Watch accounts rescued to Renew within 3 months
- Mean time to remediate top-3 technical signals
- % of renewals with explicit executive decision recorded in tracker

Quick QA checklist before an exec review
- Is the Renewal Pulse visible on slide 1?
- Are the 2 outcome metrics the customer cares about front-and-center?
- Is there one clear ask for execs (choose from the commercial options)?
- Is there an owner and deadline for each open item?

Discussion / open decisions (notes to team):
- Threshold for legal review on offers still TBD (> $200k?).
- Consider adding a Console tile for Renewal Pulse auto-calculation (product ask).
- Need a simple Google Sheet template that maps to our Salesforce fields (Marcus to prototype).

Starter links and references:
- Tracker template (copy-me): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1renewal-starter-template
- Related Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/Partnership+Review+Patterns
- Jira epic: JIRA-CS-5010 (renewal-cadence-kits)

Bottom line (TLDR):
- Keep it short: pulse + 2 metrics + one ask. Pair with a single-row tracker card and use the 60/30/14 cadence for accounts that fall into Watch/At-risk. Deck is copy-first: CSMs should adapt language for account nuance but keep structure identical across reps.

Last edits:
- v0.1 (Aisha) 2024-11-08 initial draft
- v0.2 (Aisha) 2025-03-05 added rapid playbook and starter tracker columns
